paper_metadata.title: Effect of Zr and Si addition on high temperature mechanical properties of near-α Ti–Al–Zr–Sn based alloys

evidence.quote: The mechanical properties and microstructural evolution of Ti –Al–Zr–Sn based near α-Ti alloys with various amounts of Zr and Si have been systematically investigated.

attributes.morphology: lamellar structure of α phase in α matrix

evidence.quote: the TEM image of the alloy clearly shows the lamellar structure of α phase in α matrix. In low silicon alloy, even with high Zr content (10 wt% Zr) no silicide was formed.

In Ti –7.7Al–4Zr–0.5Ta–0.5Mo–2Sn–0.05Si alloy, the high temperature compressive yielding strength was increased by about 5%, with the increase in Zr content (from 4 wt% to 10 wt%) which is mainly due to the solid solution strengthening effect.
The silicide provides dispersion hardening by acting as a barrier for the dislocation movement

Therefore, there are more barriers for dislocation motion in high Zr alloy. So, this might be one of the reasons in high Zr alloys to exhibit high compressive strength both at room temperature and at 650 1C.

mechanisms.name: reduced Si solubility in Ti by Zr addition

evidence.quote: Due to the decrease in solubility of Si in high Zr alloy (Ti –7.7Al–10Zr–0.5Ta–0.5Mo–2Sn–0.3Si), more silicide precipitates show at the α-lath boundaries.
However, at high temperature the hindrance of dislocation movement was overcome by thermal energy [31], so the strengthening effect at 650 1C was not as effective as at room temperature.
